what_it_does: Proves target is non-production, migrations are current, L0 reference data is present and unmutated
guard: Refuses any host not on the allowlist; refuses NODE_ENV=production; refuses if the project ref matches the production ref

what_it_does: Runs modules 01→14 in DAG order, writing L1→L2→L3 with uuidv5 IDs derived from the batch id
guard: Registers the batch in seed_runs as in_progress before the first write
failure_behaviour: Marks the batch partial and stops; already-written rows stay valid and removable

what_it_does: Writes the manifest to product-contract/evidence/seed-runs/<batch>.json with exact row IDs per table
failure_behaviour: A run with no manifest cannot be unloaded — the loader fails rather than skip it

what_it_does: Referential integrity, RLS spot-checks as each persona, and one assertion per screen row in the screen map
failure_behaviour: Reports which screens are still empty and why

what_it_does: Lists every batch: id, label, profile, anchor date, status, row counts
Prints exactly which tables and how many rows WOULD be deleted, in reverse-DAG order
Deletes L4-removable → L3 → L2 → L1 strictly in reverse dependency order, by explicit row ID from the manifest
guard: Refuses a batch id absent from seed_runs; refuses to delete any row not named in the manifest
failure_behaviour: Stops at the first orphan reference and reports it

what_it_does: Marks seed_runs.status = cleaned and keeps the registry row so the batch id can never be reused
Unloads every batch whose status is completed or partial, newest first — this is the whole-data unload
guard: Same guards; still never touches L0 or audit_events
